**Complete-period energy scale (successor clarification).** On $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$, $\langle x,y\rangle_{\mathrm{sum}}=\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}x(t)\overline{y(t)}$ and $\|x\|_{\mathrm{sum}}^2=\sum_t|x(t)|^2$. Unqualified $E_q^{\mathrm{full}}=\|P_qx\|_{\mathrm{sum}}^2$ and $E_q^{\mathrm{line}}=|\langle x,c_q\rangle_{\mathrm{sum}}|^2/\|c_q\|_{\mathrm{sum}}^2$ use this sum scale, as in Theorem 4.6. The corresponding mean powers are $E_q^{\mathrm{full,mean}}=E_q^{\mathrm{full}}/N$ and $E_q^{\mathrm{line,mean}}=E_q^{\mathrm{line}}/N$; the projectors do not change. For the unnormalized DFT $X(k)=\sum_t x(t)e^{-2\pi i kt/N}$ and exact conductor $\operatorname{ord}_N(k)=N/\gcd(k,N)$ (with $\gcd(0,N)=N$), $E_q^{\mathrm{full}}(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{\operatorname{ord}_N(k)=q}|X(k)|^2$, while $E_q^{\mathrm{full,mean}}(x)=N^{-2}\sum_{\operatorname{ord}_N(k)=q}|X(k)|^2$. Complete-residue orthogonality gives $\|c_q\|_{\mathrm{sum}}^2=N\varphi(q)$. These conventions concern complete periods; windowed measurements retain the separate declaration rule above.

**Finite derivation and classicality (successor correction).** A frequency of exact conductor $q$ is $k=(n/q)a$, with $a$ a unit modulo $q$. Reduction from units modulo $n$ to units modulo $q$ has uniform fiber size $\varphi(n)/\varphi(q)$, and the unit Ramanujan sum is $\mu(q)$; hence its unnormalized Fourier coefficient is $X(k)=\mu(q)\varphi(n)/\varphi(q)$, constant on the $\varphi(q)$ frequencies of this conductor. Inverting the DFT gives $P_q\chi_n=\mu(q)\varphi(n)c_q/(n\varphi(q))$, so full and line projections agree for $\chi_n$. On the **complete residue system** $s=0,\ldots,n-1$, character orthogonality gives $\sum_s|c_q(s)|^2=n\varphi(q)$ and, more generally, $\langle c_q,c_r\rangle_{\mathrm{sum}}=n\varphi(q)\delta_{q,r}$ for $q,r\mid n$. The unit-restricted norm is instead $\varphi(n)\mu(q)^2$, and unit-restricted channels are generally not orthogonal. Substituting the complete-residue norm proves the sum formula; dividing by $n$ gives the mean formula. This is a finite derivation from classical identities, with the existing `unconditional` status and `adapted` provenance tag unchanged. The predecessor's paper-specific historical attributions have not been independently verified here; no literature verification or novelty claim is added. Full proofs and conventions are in [harmonic conventions](working/00-harmonic-conventions.md), [coprime calibration](working/03-coprime-calibration.md), and [complete-residue orthogonality](working/03-ramanujan-orthogonality.md).

**Interpretive Note 9.4b (Farey Boundary Hypothesis, preserved, interpretive).** The kernel identifies the FVLT carrier axis with the Farey spine (Part II / II.13), connects Vernier phasors to Ford circles (Part II / II.5), and places the Farey tessellation in the upper half-plane (Part II / II.4). The Dirichlet-type weighting identification (Remark 5.4b) shows that negative $\alpha_{\mathrm{Tilt}}$ moves the walk's weighting law into the convergent half-plane of $\zeta(s)$, where arithmetic structure dominates.

**Hypothesis.** Negative $\alpha_{\mathrm{Tilt}}$ performs *rational descent* — motion toward the Farey boundary of the instrument, not merely visual contraction. Specifically:
$$
\alpha_{\mathrm{Tilt}} < 0 \implies \text{walk privileges low-denominator rational closure scaffold}.
$$

Under this reading: positive $\alpha_{\mathrm{Tilt}}$ — harmonic proliferation, richer interior texture; $\alpha_{\mathrm{Tilt}} = 0$ — boundary between expanding-sum and convergent-sum regimes; negative $\alpha_{\mathrm{Tilt}}$ — rational descent toward boundary-organized rational closure.

**Testable predictions.** If the hypothesis is correct, negative $\alpha_{\mathrm{Tilt}}$ should produce: (1) greater concentration of walk-derived $E_q$ in low-denominator divisor channels; (2) stronger or cleaner throat localization on rational grids in spin/$N$ space; (3) larger divergence between single-evaluation $E_q$ and walk-derived $E_q$; (4) enhanced complement diagnostics ($\mathrm{ce}_z$, $\beta$) in regimes the plan flags as exterior structure.

**Kill condition.** The hypothesis is weakened if negative $\alpha_{\mathrm{Tilt}}$ produces only visual contraction with no corresponding change in the channel structure — i.e., if walk-derived $E_q$ distributions are statistically indistinguishable across $\alpha_{\mathrm{Tilt}}$ values after normalization.

replacements.old: **(a) The signature-shape axis is a computational-cost axis.** *[interpretive]* The Part III / III.1 signature-shape classification (constant / strictly-decreasing / general-weakly-decreasing / non-monotone) and the closed/strained partition (Rmk 9.7e; III.2–III.3) sort atoms by geometric strain. They equally sort atoms by symmetry-collapse depth. A constant signature gives the full $S_m$ automorphism, so a separable equivariant quantity computes from one representative per $S_m$-orbit of exponent vectors — in the squarefree (Boolean) sub-family these orbits are the $\Omega$-rank levels with binomial sizes $\binom{m}{j}$. A weakly-decreasing signature gives the Young subgroup $\prod_i S_{m_i}$, so the computation collapses to one representative per *distinct* exponent. An atom's symmetry-speedup class is therefore fixed by its position on the III.1 signature-shape axis and is readable from $\sigma(N)$ before any computation runs. This is the Note 9.7m position-awareness property (Part II / II.18) lifted one level — from intra-atom position to inter-atom cost class.
replacements.new: **(a) Symmetry cost depends on the actual orbit action.** *[conditional workload statement]* For the fixed exponent word $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$, the lattice automorphism group permutes only equal-length prime-power chains: $G_a=\prod_v S_{m_v}$, where $m_v=|\{i:a_i=v\}|$. On divisor exponent vectors $e$ with $0\leq e_i\leq a_i$, an invariant scalar workload can use one representative per $G_a$-orbit; the orbit representatives are multisets of $m_v$ values from $0,\ldots,v$ for each $v$, giving $\prod_v\binom{m_v+v}{v}$ orbits. The full vector count is $\tau(N)=\prod_v(v+1)^{m_v}$. A saving follows only when the requested statistic is invariant and its per-orbit aggregation is cheaper than full evaluation. Monotonicity labels (constant, decreasing, nonmonotone) alone do not determine the cost; the exponent multiplicity partition and workload do.

replacements.old: **(b) Profile-class transport.** *[unconditional core; transport reading operational]* Define the *profile class* of an atom $\mathrm{Div}(N)$ as the multiset $\{a_i\}$ of its exponent signature $\sigma(N)$. By unique factorization and Birkhoff duality (Aut of a finite distributive lattice $=$ Aut of its poset of join-irreducibles; for $\mathrm{Div}(N)$ the join-irreducibles are the prime-power chains), **any two atoms in the same profile class have isomorphic divisor lattices** — hence identical automorphism group $\prod_i S_{m_i}$, identical Thm K.2 Cartesian-product structure, identical closed/strained status, identical apex defect $\delta_{\mathrm{apex}}$, **and identical ambient cyclotomic field-of-definition bound $L = \mathrm{lcm}(m, n_0, \ldots, n_{m-1})$ for $\delta_{\mathrm{apex}}$ (Lemma 9.7q, Part II / II.15)**. *Profile class $=$ isomorphism class of atoms.* Rmk 9.7f records the single instance $\mathrm{Div}(30) \cong \mathrm{Div}(1001)$ (shared profile $(1,1,1)$); §10.8(b) is that statement made atlas-general.
replacements.new: **(b) Profile-class transport.** *[unconditional lattice core; geometry excluded]* Define the *profile class* by the unordered exponent multiset $\{a_i\}$. Two atoms in one class have isomorphic divisor lattices, the same Cartesian-product path factors, divisor count, rank polynomial, and automorphism-group type $\prod_vS_{m_v}$. These are invariants of the unordered profile. The §9.7 apex defect and closed/strained status also use the ordered exponent word in fixed canonical prime-rank seats; they do not follow from lattice isomorphism or the unordered profile. The ambient conductor expression $L=\operatorname{lcm}(m,n_0,\ldots,n_{m-1})$ is profile invariant as an upper field bound, even though the actual apex value need not be. The example $\mathrm{Div}(30)\cong\mathrm{Div}(1001)$ illustrates the lattice claim.
